title: Have you ever created simpler browser games?
author: BroPleaseListenToMe
selftext:
I’d be curious whether you’ve ever created browser games similar to the ones popular in the 2010s, like Travian, Ikariam, Shakes & Fidget, Gladiatus, etc.

If yes, which AI model did you use, and how did you create the beautiful game HUDs, characters, building models, and other visual assets so they looked polished and unique?

comments.author: Old_Ktulu
comments.body: I have a game idea that i began to draft a few days ago and currently asking myself what would be the best way to release it between browser or mobile app. Do ppl even play browser games like we used too 10+ years ago ?

replies.author: BroPleaseListenToMe
replies.body: Most companies that built browser games back then have either moved to mobile platforms or gone bankrupt. Browser games are no longer as popular as they used to be, but I still believe that a good and engaging browser game (especially one with its own app or a responsive mobile-friendly design) could attract a solid player base and generate noticeable revenue as well.

replies.author: MinimusMaximizer
replies.body: Everything is driven by the platform algorithms now. It's no longer organic. A strong enough signal could break through that, but you'd be fighting a tsunami of a tide. My real issue with AI is that platforming is that it relentlessly drives everything to the median for maximum engagement. But if you're doing it for fun, the money might happen, just don't count on it, you're working the graveyard shift of the web.

replies.author: AdrianRWalker
replies.body:
Most people that play browser games fall into 2 categories. Adults looking to kill time when on the computer, likely at work with downtime. Or. Young kids, where parents don’t want to spend money on Console games and who don’t want kids on the phone. 

If your game can hit ether of those then your golden.

comments.author: MinimusMaximizer
comments.body: Broadly, you can create anything in the browser today that would have pushed the HW in the 1990s with ease, with 2026 resolution and framerate for no additional charge. As for making real money off it, well, that's about as likely as becoming the next Mr. Beast, so either don't it for the money, or OCD A/B test every aspect until you hit liftoff like he did.
